subject: SOC 2 access artifacts request — SCIM / SAML / RBAC & fallback justification
messages:
From: Lisa Morgan <lisa@brightpath.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medisphere.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jul 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2 access artifacts request — SCIM/SAML/RBAC

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the quick kickoff call this morning. MediSphere's SOC 2 reviewer asked us to pull a minimal set of artifacts to validate access control controls (CC6/CC7 equivalents). Could you provide the following sample artifacts for our audit intake? We're only looking for samples, not full logs at this stage.

Requested items (samples):
- SCIM delta snapshots for the last 90 days (CSV or JSON fine) showing adds/updates/removals with timestamps and actor id.
- SAML assertion samples covering recent user logins (include signed assertion times, audience, and NameID).
- RBAC role matrix (mapping role -> permissions, number of active users) and a short justification of least-privilege decisions for privileged roles (service accounts, admins).
- Note about fallback/degenerate access paths: provide any documented fallback/delegation policy (e.g., emergency admin process) and a short trace showing how it's audited.

We prefer redacted samples (hashed emails ok) but need real timestamps and event ids. If you have a suggested delivery plan (what you can deliver and when), send it over.

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Morgan
Senior Assur. Manager, Brightpath Consulting
lisa@brightpath.com

--

Subject: Re: SOC2 access artifacts request — SCIM/SAML/RBAC

Hi Lisa — thanks for the list and the clear ask. We're able to produce redacted SCIM deltas and SAML assertion samples. Quick clarifying questions before we start pulling artifacts:

1) For SCIM deltas, do you need full attribute lists or just identity key changes (email, active, groups)? We can do a full delta but it adds time for PII redaction.
2) For SAML assertions, should we include only human-user assertions or also app/service assertions (some internal service accounts authenticate via SAML for certain legacy apps)?

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- By Tue 15 Jul: initial redacted SCIM delta (90d) + 10 SAML assertion samples (human users)
- By Thu 17 Jul: RBAC role matrix and least-priv justification for privileged roles (service accounts + admin roles)
- By Mon 21 Jul: fallback/delegation policy excerpt + a short audit trace (one-week window)

We'll attach filename stubs and a shared Drive folder once we start the export. If that schedule is tight for your reviewer please flag which items are highest priority.

Thanks — looping in Laura (security ops) and Aditya (customer success / intake) to help coordinate the exports and redaction.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Soojin / Aditya — quick operational notes to avoid rework: 

- Redaction: Hashing emails + removing user display names is acceptable. Keep internal actor ids intact (uid_xxx).
- SCIM: include group membership deltas for any role-bearing groups (admin, infra, billing) — auditors look for group->role links.
- SAML: pick assertions spanning 3 different IdP binding times (peak, off-peak, and a weekend) to show variety. Include the Audience and AuthnContext. Remove the full certificate blobs; a cert fingerprint is fine.
- RBAC matrix: include a short column for "justification" (why each role exists) and one for "last review date". If we don't have a recent manual review, note the automated role owner assignment process.
- Fallback/delegation: provide the emergency access ticket template (redact requester name) and the Jira ticket id pattern — auditors like an example trace.

If exports will touch production logs, schedule a maintenance window with infra. Otherwise use our analytics export layer. I'll draft the redaction rules and drop them in the shared Drive folder this morning: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxx-Redwood/SOC2-Artifact-Uploads

Laura Bennett
Head of Security Operations
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
